title: Rolling ridge forecasts failed to beat zero in an ETF return backtest
summary: In a 2005–2025 ETF study, a rolling ridge model using past return features produced negative mean out-of-sample R² at every tested regularization level against a zero-return forecast. Scores approached zero as stronger regularization shrank the predictions.
organization: KTH Royal Institute of Technology; Stanford University

source_review.scope: §§2, 5.3 and 6.3, Figure 25 and the disclosed universe selection

evidence.tested: The model was repeatedly fitted on trailing observations and scored on the following period. The paper compared multiple regularization levels with a zero forecast.
evidence.unknown: The ETFs were selected from ones still trading at study time, producing survivorship bias. The result concerns the chosen predictors, horizons and historical universe.
evidence.ai_role: The fitted regression generated return forecasts from past observations, enabling a retrospective comparison of predictive signal against the zero baseline.
